key_insight: TideSand multiplexes sandbox resources to increase LLM-agent throughput while preserving tool-call fidelity for performance-sensitive tasks.
engineering_relevance: Agent infrastructure can improve resource utilization without sacrificing the measurement accuracy needed for automated systems research.
method: Agent-aware scheduling coordinates tool calls to avoid resource contention.
Speculative swapping offloads sandbox memory during inference waits and restores it before the next tool call.
Selective rollback checkpoints chosen sandboxes during contention and restores them when machines are idle.
evidence_signal: Across six model-workload pairs on AlgoTune, Terminal-Bench 4.0, and Terminal-Bench Science, TideSand reports 3.8–10× higher throughput than strict reservation while maintaining fidelity, or 7–44% higher fidelity than overcommit baselines at similar throughput, plus a 19× reduction in AlgoTune evaluation error.
watch_item: Deployment should validate whether swap and checkpoint overheads remain manageable under different workloads and hardware.
paper_title: TideSand: Performance-Accurate Sandbox Multiplexing for LLM Agents
